alternatives.label: Earth systems, economics and sustainable development
alternatives.concept: Combines Earth and climate science, soils and aquifers, biodiversity foundations and sustainability governance with economics and quantitative methods. GIS, field activities and a team delta research project connect physical evidence with social decisions. This is substantial related study, with gaps in dedicated environmental economics, technical spatial planning, VU fieldwork and an individual thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule spans Earth science, water, climate, resources, economics, spatial data and policy; the title describes its actual interdisciplinary core.
progression: Introductory Earth systems, economics and sustainability precede GIS, hydrology and upper-level geochemistry, economics and research; prerequisites and term offerings pass.

alternatives.label: Resources, energy and environmental economics
alternatives.concept: Examines resources and energy through Earth science, soils and aquifers, ecology, circular recovery, resource research and renewable-system design. Five economics courses provide 37.5 EC of economic theory, public policy and empirical analysis, compared with 22.5 EC in the closest programme. Applications to sustainability are supported by the science and governance courses; general economics courses are not renamed environmental economics.
alternatives.labelReason: Economics, resource geoscience, circularity, renewable design, governance and behavioural choice form the scheduled focus.
progression: Gateway sustainability and chemistry/material foundations, Dynamic Earth and Soils & Aquifers precede advanced biogeochemistry/resource work. Statistics precedes econometrics; microeconomics is taken after the methods gateway. All24placements use actual assigned-term offerings; nine300-level courses.
alternatives.distinctness: The programmes share20courses; each has4courses(30EC) absent from the other. The closest combines hazards, water management, biodiversity and environmental justice. This direction instead adds macroeconomics, public economics, ecosystem modelling and renewable-system design. The economic weighting and technical energy question substantiate the distinction beyond the numerical threshold.

candidates.label: Flood adaptation and spatial environmental data

routeSelection.route: Ordinary 180-EC full-time bachelor under the adopted 2026–27 OER; first-listed 6-EC third-year restricted elective Stedelijke uitdagingen
routeSelection.basis: The standard full-time bachelor has no formal specialisation to select. Its third-year restricted choice is 6 EC from Stedelijke uitdagingen or a 6-EC thesis extension; the first-listed urban course is selected in source order without reference to UCR fit. The 30-EC genuinely open minor space is not treated as compulsory geography coursework.

selection.assessment: Retain two substantive responses: integrated Earth/economics sustainability and resource/energy economics. The flood/data candidate shares20of24courses with the closest; its added general modelling/ML/public economics/renewable design does not supply a sufficiently distinct hydrology or spatial-adaptation sequence. The closest already covers water/soil/GIS/fieldwork interests. Numerical four-course difference alone does not establish academic distinctness. No third programme manufactured. The AI interest is accounted for within the rejected data candidate, not claimed as a capability of the closest programme.

blocks: Earth systems, water, climate risk and spatial fieldwork
Both address global climatic change; UCR emphasizes anthropogenic climate impacts.
Both introduce interacting Earth systems and field observation.
This specified VU unit is not supplied as a dedicated course in the retained UCR schedules. Related foundations do not imply full equivalence.
Both investigate soils, hydrology and the landscape through field/lab methods.
Both study water management; UCR is focused on deltas and flood adaptation.
Both train in GIS and Earth-observation datasets.
Both analyse natural hazards and risk reduction.
VU has a specified first-year climate-adaptation field course; related UCR field activities are not the same credited placement.
VU requires its own specified 6-EC spatial-solutions fieldwork; UCR delta research and field activities are related, not an exact equivalent.
Land, ecology, energy and sustainability governance
Both engage environmental constraints on land use, though UCR emphasizes ecology rather than land-use planning.
Both examine lower-carbon energy transition; UCR designs renewable systems.
Both examine energy and Earth resources; UCR focuses on geoscience research.
Both concern biodiversity, but UCR teaches biological diversity and investigation rather than VU nature-management practice.
Both address planning and collective decisions about sustainability; UCR emphasizes policy governance, not technical spatial planning.
Both examine environmental values and responsibilities, but UCR frames them through social movements and environmental justice rather than professional ethics.
Economic choices, environmental value and policy
Both teach economic foundations of choices under scarcity.
Both provide mathematics for environmental/economic quantitative work.
Both examine socio-economic choices under scarcity, though UCR focuses on microeconomics and behaviour.
Both can analyse environmental externalities and public economics; UCR does not offer a dedicated environmental-economics course.
Chosen 6-EC urban challenges module remains programme-specific; related sustainability governance and economics courses are not the same urban module.
Quantitative methods, interdisciplinary research and open space
Both plan/applied research for a sustainability question, but UCR project is not VU fieldwork preparation.
Both use statistical analysis, with UCR teaching general probability and statistics.
UCR includes data cleaning, visualisation and spatial datasets; it is introductory general data science rather than VU advanced sustainability Big Data.
The compulsory independent 12-EC VU bachelor thesis cannot be counted as an ordinary UCR course or UCR’s optional research element.
Genuine open 30-EC minor space remains student-selected and is not a fixed external course to align.

notes.text: Both UCR programmes sustain Earth, sustainability and economic study. They leave gaps in dedicated environmental economics, technical spatial planning and VU’s two specified fieldwork units and required individual 12 EC thesis. UCR field/lab activities and team delta research are genuine related experience. Optional independent research, shown separately, requires approval and is outside the 24-course schedules; it does not replace the VU thesis.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Earth Sciences, Economics and Sustainability connects physical Earth systems with economic choices and spatial sustainability problems. Students study climate risk, water, land, energy and resources using field research, data analysis and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR programme combines Earth and climate science, soils, water, biodiversity and governance with economics and quantitative methods. The second gives greater weight to economics and focuses on resources and renewable energy. Both offer substantive related study while leaving gaps in dedicated environmental economics, spatial planning, VU fieldwork and the required individual thesis. These programmes do not provide a dedicated environmental AI pathway.

curriculum.routeLabel: Ordinary full-time bachelor; Urban Challenges restricted elective
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 144 EC of required courses, one 6 EC restricted choice and 30 EC of free study. Fieldwork preparation requires 24 eligible first-year EC; second-year fieldwork requires 60 EC including the first fieldwork. Thesis entry requires 126 EC including recognised fieldwork. Free-choice courses have level and approval rules. The first-year study-advice norm is 42 EC. A language test or remediation gates the Soil and Landscape grade; mentoring and Geoflex obligations carry no credits.
